details: Planetary-scale 3D reconstruction via oblique photogrammetry/LiDAR is prohibitively costly and slow, while existing outdoor scene generators rely on synthetic or hallucinated content and cannot deliver real-world, geospatially anchored, interactive Earth-scale 3D.
Need a conditioning signal that exists everywhere on Earth: standard geo-referenced satellite imagery, without known acquisition angles or multi-view overlap.

ABot-Earth 0.5: a generative 3D framework that synthesizes scenes natively in the 3D Gaussian Splatting representation (compression into a latent space of real-world 3DGS tiles, then generation directly back into 3DGS), conditioned on satellite imagery.

Four coupled mechanisms: native 3DGS generative modeling trained on real reconstructions; a decoder that inherently emits a hierarchical multi-LOD 3DGS structure; sliding-window inference that blends overlapping tiles for seamless large-area coherence; cross-domain conditioning (simulated satellite renders at training + VLM-based adaptation harness at inference).

Training data are city-scale real-world 3DGS scenes reconstructed by the in-house ABot-3DGS engine from satellite (multi-stereo, via FromOrbit2Ground), oblique aerial, and street/drone urban imagery; proprietary plus public sets (DFC 2019, UrbanScene3D, UrbanBIS, Mill-19, UC-GS, etc.).

Sliding-window spatial partitioning into overlapping 200m x 200m tiles, normalized and cluster-cleaned; multi-view virtual camera arrays across altitude layers, nadir-to-oblique pitches and multiple yaws, plus simulated satellite-view renders as conditioning.

Three-level quality control: tile-level (PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS, geometric accuracy, VLM perceptual score, completeness), view-level (opacity filtering + VLM scoring), dataset-level (stratified spatial diversity balancing and embedding-space semantic deduplication).

A100 GPU inference: 4K satellite image per pass covers ~1.6km x 1.6km (2.56 km2), 64x the training tile area; ~25 min per tile; ~312,500 tiles cover ~800,000 km2 of global built-up area; <10 days on a 1,000-GPU cluster.
Web Mercator (EPSG:3857) tiles mosaicked and isotropically resampled to a uniform GSD matching training scale; outputs transformed into per-tile ENU frames with global georeferencing.

LOD reorganization into map tile hierarchy zoom 14-19: zoom 17-19 generated natively by the model, zoom 14-16 by CPU-side statistical decimation using Bhattacharyya distance; OGC 3D Tiles tileset.json plus implicit {zoom}/{x}/{y} paths; rendered by the Amap Yunjing engine with viewport-dependent streaming.

Generative fidelity: FID and KID between 2D renderings of generated scenes and ground truth renderings from real-world 3DGS reconstructions; baselines CityDreamer, GaussianCity, EarthCrafter (numbers cited from their papers).

System-level: comparison against Google Earth and Marble on spatial coverage, timeliness/efficiency, visual quality, and openness; human study rating geometric accuracy, textural fidelity, and overall aesthetics.

Extension experiment: COLMAP SfM/MVS reconstructions of landmarks (Eiffel Tower, Colosseum, US Capitol, Arc de Triomphe) from crowd-sourced imagery converted to 3DGS, geo-registered and composited into generated scenes.

key_findings.finding: Native 3DGS generation conditioned on satellite imagery substantially outperforms prior outdoor scene generators in rendering realism.
key_findings.evidence: FID of 16.1 versus the previous best reported 69.5 among CityDreamer, GaussianCity and EarthCrafter, with the ground-truth distribution taken from renderings of complex real-world 3DGS reconstructions rather than synthetic data.

key_findings.finding: The framework makes Earth-scale 3D content production practical at a cost/latency far below photogrammetry.
key_findings.evidence: Under 10 minutes per km2 from satellite imagery alone; the deployed pipeline covers ~800,000 km2 in ~312,500 tiles, estimated under 10 days on 1,000 GPUs, versus months-to-years update cycles for commercial photogrammetric pipelines; launch spans 300+ cities in 190+ countries.

key_findings.finding: Trillion-primitive generated 3DGS can be streamed interactively by reusing standard map-engine tile scheduling, thanks to natively generated LOD.
key_findings.evidence: ~3.2 trillion Gaussians across ~320,000 blocks organized into a 6-level zoom 14-19 hierarchy (top three levels emitted natively by the decoder, lower levels via analytic Bhattacharyya-distance decimation on CPU in parallel with GPU inference), rendered in real time in the Amap Yunjing engine with frustum culling, asynchronous streaming and fade transitions.

key_findings.finding: Generated scenes are aesthetically competitive with, but geometrically less accurate than, photogrammetric Google Earth, while covering regions Google Earth lacks.
key_findings.evidence: Human study radar results show a higher overall aesthetics score than Google Earth but lower geometric accuracy and textural fidelity; a continental-scale comparison shows plausible 3D generation over Ireland where Google Earth falls back to 2D imagery.

key_findings.finding: Because output is native 3DGS, generated environments are composable with independently reconstructed high-fidelity assets.
key_findings.evidence: COLMAP-based dense reconstructions of four landmarks converted to 3DGS, geo-registered and composited into the generated context, preserving fine architectural detail while blending with surroundings.
